The longest scripts in my folder did no spatial analysis at all: they built an **information note** in
PDF, with logos, a legend, a table per protected area and the text of each occurrence. That was 1,500
lines of `fpdf`, and any layout change was a chore.

Here is the same kind of product, a **deforestation bulletin per protected area** with public data, in
four ways. The easiest to maintain is usually **Quarto**: the layout lives in a text file and the script
only changes the protected area.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}

:::

## What goes into the bulletin

1. **Period** and source, computed from the data itself (never typed in).
2. **Summary table**: area of alerts inside and around each protected area.
3. A **chart** of the table.
4. **One page per protected area**, with the map from the [previous article](10-automated-maps.qmd).

The data come from the `deter_interior_entorno` layer (article [Inside and around](02-inside-and-around.qmd)):
deforestation alerts (clear-cut, with vegetation and mining) from the last 90 days.

## The code

Names in Portuguese: `boletim` = bulletin, `relatorio` = report, `tabela` = table, `grafico` = chart,
`inicio`/`fim` = start/end, `nome` = name.

::: {.panel-tabset group="programa"}

## ArcGIS Pro

ArcGIS Pro has **Reports** (Insert → Report), which build the table per protected area with header and
footer, and **Map Series** in the layout. The script combines both into a PDF:

```python
import arcpy

projeto = arcpy.mp.ArcGISProject(r"C:\dados\boletim.aprx")

# Table by protected area (report created in Insert → Report, grouped by nome_uc)
relatorio = projeto.listReports("Alertas por UC")[0]
relatorio.exportToPDF(r"C:\dados\saida\tabela.pdf")

# One map per protected area (layout with a map series set up)
layout = projeto.listLayouts("Mapa por UC")[0]
layout.mapSeries.exportToPDF(r"C:\dados\saida\mapas.pdf")

# Join everything into a single file
boletim = arcpy.mp.PDFDocumentCreate(r"C:\dados\saida\boletim.pdf")
boletim.appendPages(r"C:\dados\saida\tabela.pdf")
boletim.appendPages(r"C:\dados\saida\mapas.pdf")
boletim.saveAndClose()
```

The `fpdf2` code from the Python tab also runs in ArcGIS Pro: in the **Package Manager**, clone the
default environment, activate the clone and install `fpdf2`. That is how the original scripts worked.

## QGIS

The QGIS Atlas exports **one PDF with one page per protected area**. Just add to the layout from the
[previous article](10-automated-maps.qmd) an **attribute table** filtered by the page's protected area.
Run this snippet **after** the code from that article:

```python
# Continues the code from the previous article (layout, atlas and layers already created)
from qgis.core import QgsLayoutItemAttributeTable, QgsLayoutFrame, QgsLayoutItemPage

# Shrink the map to make room for the table below, in portrait
layout.pageCollection().page(0).setPageSize("A4", QgsLayoutItemPage.Portrait)
mapa.attemptResize(QgsLayoutSize(194, 150, MM))
mapa.zoomToExtent(para_metros.transformBoundingBox(extensao_ucs))
legenda.setColumnCount(2)
for item, (x, y) in [(legenda, (8, 176)), (norte, (188, 25)), (escala, (145, 178)),
                     (fonte, (145, 192))]:
    item.attemptMove(QgsLayoutPoint(x, y, MM))
norte.attemptResize(QgsLayoutSize(11, 11, MM))
fonte.attemptResize(QgsLayoutSize(57, 20, MM))

# Table with the alerts of the page's protected area (filtered by the atlas feature)
tabela = QgsLayoutItemAttributeTable.create(layout)
layout.addMultiFrame(tabela)                 # the layout now owns the table
tabela.setVectorLayer(alertas)
tabela.setFilterFeatures(True)
tabela.setFeatureFilter('intersects($geometry, @atlas_geometry)')
tabela.setMaximumNumberOfFeatures(10)
tabela.setDisplayedFields(["view_date", "classname", "municipality"])
quadro_tabela = QgsLayoutFrame(layout, tabela)
tabela.addFrame(quadro_tabela)
quadro_tabela.attemptMove(QgsLayoutPoint(8, 230, MM))
quadro_tabela.attemptResize(QgsLayoutSize(194, 58, MM))

# A single PDF, with one page per protected area
config_pdf = QgsLayoutExporter.PdfExportSettings()
resultado, erro = QgsLayoutExporter.exportToPdf(atlas, PASTA + "boletim_qgis.pdf", config_pdf)
print("PDF:", "ok" if resultado == QgsLayoutExporter.Success else erro)
```

The filter `intersects($geometry, @atlas_geometry)` makes the table show only the alerts of the page's
protected area. Without code, the same filter is in **Item Properties → Filter with**.

## PostGIS

The database delivers the table ready for any report generator (Quarto, Power BI, ArcGIS Pro):

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW artigos.boletim_90_dias AS
WITH periodo AS (SELECT max(view_date) AS fim FROM artigos.deter_interior_entorno)
SELECT nome_uc,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE local = 'interior')                 AS alertas_interior,
       round(sum(area_ha) FILTER (WHERE local = 'interior'), 1)   AS interior_ha,
       round(sum(area_ha) FILTER (WHERE local = 'entorno'), 1)    AS entorno_ha,
       min(p.fim) - 90 AS inicio, min(p.fim) AS fim
FROM artigos.deter_interior_entorno, periodo p
WHERE classname IN ('DESMATAMENTO_CR', 'DESMATAMENTO_VEG', 'MINERACAO')
  AND view_date > p.fim - 90
GROUP BY nome_uc
ORDER BY interior_ha DESC NULLS LAST;

SELECT * FROM artigos.boletim_90_dias;
```

## Python

With **fpdf2** (`pip install fpdf2`), the same package as the original scripts:

```python
from datetime import date
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from fpdf import FPDF

CLASSES = ["DESMATAMENTO_CR", "DESMATAMENTO_VEG", "MINERACAO"]

def nome(texto):
    """FLORESTA NACIONAL DO JAMANXIM -> Floresta Nacional do Jamanxim"""
    return " ".join(p if p in ("de", "do", "da", "dos", "das", "e") else p.capitalize()
                    for p in texto.lower().split())

# 1. Data: deforestation alerts from the last 90 days, by protected area and zone
d = gpd.read_file("dados/deter_interior_entorno.gpkg")
d["view_date"] = pd.to_datetime(d["view_date"])
fim = d["view_date"].max()
inicio = fim - pd.Timedelta(days=90)
d = d[d["classname"].isin(CLASSES) & (d["view_date"] > inicio)]
tabela = (d.pivot_table(index="nome_uc", columns="local", values="area_ha",
                        aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)
          .reindex(columns=["interior", "entorno"], fill_value=0)
          .sort_values("interior", ascending=False))
alertas = d[d["local"] == "interior"].groupby("nome_uc").size()

# 2. Chart for the report
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.2))
tabela[::-1].rename(index=nome).plot.barh(ax=ax, color=["#009E73", "#E69F00"], width=0.75)
ax.set_xlabel("Area of alerts (ha)")
ax.set_ylabel("")
ax.legend(["Inside", "3 km surroundings"], frameon=False)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("dados/boletim_grafico.png", dpi=200)

# 3. The PDF: header and footer on every page
class Boletim(FPDF):
    def header(self):
        self.set_fill_color(0, 114, 178)
        self.set_text_color(255)
        self.set_font("Helvetica", "B", 13)
        self.cell(0, 10, "  Deforestation bulletin for protected areas",
                  fill=True, new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")
        self.set_text_color(0)
        self.ln(3)

    def footer(self):
        self.set_y(-12)
        self.set_font("Helvetica", "", 8)
        self.cell(0, 6, f"Sources: INPE (DETER), MMA (CNUC). Generated on "
                        f"{date.today():%Y-%m-%d}.", align="L")
        self.cell(0, 6, f"Page {self.page_no()}", align="R")

pdf = Boletim(orientation="P", unit="mm", format="A4")
pdf.set_auto_page_break(auto=True, margin=15)
pdf.add_page()

# 4. Summary, table and chart
pdf.set_font("Helvetica", "", 11)
pdf.multi_cell(0, 6, f"DETER deforestation alerts (clear-cut, with vegetation and mining) "
                     f"between {inicio:%Y-%m-%d} and {fim:%Y-%m-%d}, inside the protected areas "
                     f"and in the 3 km band around them.")
pdf.ln(3)
pdf.set_font("Helvetica", "", 9)
with pdf.table(col_widths=(90, 25, 35, 35), text_align=("LEFT", "RIGHT", "RIGHT", "RIGHT")) as t:
    t.row(["Protected area", "Alerts", "Inside (ha)", "Surroundings (ha)"])
    for uc, linha in tabela.iterrows():
        t.row([nome(uc), str(alertas.get(uc, 0)),
               f"{linha['interior']:,.1f}", f"{linha['entorno']:,.1f}"])
pdf.ln(4)
pdf.image("dados/boletim_grafico.png", w=180)

# 5. One page per protected area, with the map from the previous article
ucs = gpd.read_file("dados/artigos.gpkg", layer="ucs").set_index("nome_uc")
for uc in tabela.index:
    pdf.add_page()
    pdf.set_font("Helvetica", "B", 12)
    pdf.cell(0, 8, nome(uc), new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")
    pdf.set_font("Helvetica", "", 10)
    pdf.cell(0, 6, f"{ucs.loc[uc, 'categoria']} · {ucs.loc[uc, 'grupo']} · "
                   f"CNUC {ucs.loc[uc, 'cnuc']}", new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")
    pdf.cell(0, 6, f"Inside: {tabela.loc[uc, 'interior']:.1f} ha · "
                   f"Surroundings: {tabela.loc[uc, 'entorno']:.1f} ha", new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")
    pdf.ln(2)
    pdf.image(f"dados/mapas_py/mapa_{ucs.loc[uc, 'cnuc']}.png", w=185)

pdf.output("dados/boletim.pdf")
print("boletim.pdf with", pdf.page_no(), "pages")
print(tabela.round(1))
```

## Quarto

A `boletim.qmd` file is the **template**; the `cnuc` parameter picks the protected area. The PDF is
produced by **Typst**, which ships with Quarto (no LaTeX needed).

````markdown
---
title: "Deforestation bulletin"
format:
  typst:
    papersize: a4
    margin: {x: 2cm, y: 2cm}
lang: en
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
jupyter: python3
---

```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]
cnuc = "0000.00.0266"      # replaced when rendering: -P cnuc:...
```

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown

def nome(texto):
    return " ".join(p if p in ("de", "do", "da", "dos", "das", "e") else p.capitalize()
                    for p in texto.lower().split())

G = "../dados/artigos.gpkg"
uc = gpd.read_file(G, layer="ucs").query("cnuc == @cnuc").iloc[0]
d = gpd.read_file("../dados/deter_interior_entorno.gpkg").query("cnuc == @cnuc")
d["view_date"] = pd.to_datetime(d["view_date"])
fim = d["view_date"].max()
d = d[d["classname"].isin(["DESMATAMENTO_CR", "DESMATAMENTO_VEG", "MINERACAO"])
      & (d["view_date"] > fim - pd.Timedelta(days=90))]
area = d.groupby("local")["area_ha"].sum().reindex(["interior", "entorno"], fill_value=0)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"## {nome(uc['nome_uc'])}\n")
print(f"{uc['categoria']} · {uc['grupo']} · CNUC {cnuc}\n")
print(f"In the 90 days up to **{fim:%Y-%m-%d}**, DETER recorded **{area['interior']:,.1f} ha** "
      f"of deforestation inside the protected area and **{area['entorno']:,.1f} ha** in the "
      f"3 km surroundings.\n")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Map of the protected area with alerts since August 2026."
from IPython.display import Image
Image(f"../dados/mapas_py/mapa_{cnuc}.png", width=600)
```

```{python}
tabela = (d.groupby(["local", "classname"])["area_ha"].agg(["count", "sum"]).round(1)
          .reset_index()
          .rename(columns={"local": "Zone", "classname": "Class",
                           "count": "Alerts", "sum": "Area (ha)"}))
Markdown(tabela.to_markdown(index=False))
```
````

To produce one PDF per protected area, call Quarto in a loop (on Windows, use a PowerShell `for`):

```bash
for cnuc in 0000.00.0266 0000.00.0267 0000.00.0268; do
  quarto render boletim.qmd -P cnuc:$cnuc --output boletim_$cnuc.pdf
done
```

Quarto needs `jupyter`, `papermill` and `tabulate` installed in the same Python as the data
(`pip install jupyter papermill tabulate`).

:::

## Checking the result

The Python (fpdf2), Quarto and QGIS versions produced PDFs with the same numbers. In the 90 days up to
2026-10-16:

| Protected area | Alerts inside | Inside (ha) | Surroundings (ha) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Jamanxim National Forest | 35 | 628.5 | 9.1 |
| Altamira National Forest | 12 | 436.1 | 24.2 |
| Tapajós Environmental Protection Area | 38 | 433.0 | 274.0 |
| Jamanxim National Park | 6 | 73.5 | 100.9 |
| Rio Novo National Park | 6 | 48.2 | 0 |

: DETER deforestation alerts (clear-cut, with vegetation and mining) in the 90 days up to 2026-10-16. {.striped}

In Jamanxim National Park, a strict-protection area, the surroundings had **more** deforestation than
the inside during the period. That is the kind of finding a weekly bulletin shows early.

## Pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning}
## Dates typed into the text
"Bulletin for September 1 to 30" typed by hand is wrong the first time the script runs in another month.
Compute the period from the data (`max(view_date)`), as in the code above.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Special characters in the PDF
fpdf2's standard fonts (Helvetica, Times) only have Latin-1 characters: accented letters work, but em
dashes (—), curly quotes and emoji do not. For any character, load a TTF font with
`pdf.add_font("DejaVu", "", "DejaVuSans.ttf")`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Attribute table in a QGIS layout, from code
Create the table with `QgsLayoutItemAttributeTable.create(layout)` and register it with
`layout.addMultiFrame(tabela)` **before** configuring it. Without that, Python deletes the table from
memory and QGIS crashes silently when exporting.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Logos and visual identity
Official bulletins carry the agency's logo and header. In a personal or study bulletin, **do not use
institutional logos**: make it clear that it is your own product, made with public data.
:::
